title: Phantom Blade Zero Endings - All 4 Endings and How to Unlock Them
description: Phantom Blade Zero has four endings, not eight. Annihilation, Long Roar, the true ending Final Battle, and the secret Undying Grudge - what each one needs, and which mistake locks you out of the platinum.
keyword: phantom blade zero endings, phantom blade zero how many endings, phantom blade zero true ending, phantom blade zero final battle, phantom blade zero undying grudge

facts.label: Number of endings
facts.value: 4 - confirmed post-launch, superseding the '8 endings' figure repeated before release

facts.label: Default ending
facts.value: Annihilation - triggers if no purple Tales are completed

facts.label: True ending
facts.value: Final Battle, called the Perfect Ending internally - needs every purple Tale done before Mount Soulrend

facts.label: Secret ending
facts.value: Undying Grudge - only from failing the 66 Days mode

facts.label: Second playthrough needed
facts.value: Only for Undying Grudge. The other three come from one save

facts.label: Trophy tie-in
facts.value: With Heart and Blood (Gold) needs the true ending; the normal ending has no trophy

facts.label: Point of no return
facts.value: The climb to Mount Soulrend, after the Mirage Estate in Pangzhen

sections.title: The Short Answer
sections.content:
Four endings. Annihilation is what you get for playing the story and nothing else. Long Roar is the middle tier, unlocked with two specific Tales. Final Battle is the true ending and needs essentially all the purple Tales plus five Lóng Pillar trials and four Acolyte masks. Undying Grudge is a separate secret, and it does not come from playing well - it comes from wiping out in the 66 Days mode.

Before release this page listed eight endings as a possibility and said none were detailed. That was wrong. IGN's post-launch ending guide puts the count at four, each with its own cutscene, and the in-game ending names match across IGN, Polygon and GamingBolt. The eight-ending figure was never sourced and has been removed from this site.

sections.title: All Four Endings
sections.content:
EndingIn-game nameWhat unlocks itTrophy
NormalAnnihilationReach the final boss without completing the purple Tales, especially Secrets at the Heart of the LakeNone
MiddleLong RoarSecrets at the Heart of the Lake plus Bloodline Awakening - all five pillars, Gold-Masked One beaten five timesNot separately tracked
TrueFinal Battle / Perfect EndingEvery purple Tale, both Crystal Puppet Eyes, the Four Guardians' Mirror realm and all five Lóng Pillars, done before the climb to Mount SoulrendWith Heart and Blood (Gold)
SecretUndying Grudge (饮恨江湖)Unlock 66 Days after any completion, then lose all 66 livesNone

Only the true ending is tied to a trophy, so a pure platinum run only has to satisfy one of these four branches. Everything above the true ending row is optional story content, not optional difficulty.

sections.title: Annihilation - the Default Ending
sections.content:
The default. Fight to the last boss and finish, without clearing the purple Tales, and the credits roll on Annihilation. Nothing is locked by choosing it - you can keep exploring after the credits - but the True Ending fight will not trigger, and several side Tales become unfinishable once Mount Soulrend is behind you.

This is the one ending with no trophy attached. If you are here for the platinum, stopping at Annihilation means a second run for the story content you skipped.

sections.title: Long Roar - the Two-Tale Ending
sections.content:
Long Roar sits between the default and the true ending, and it is the one the guides disagree about least. The two requirements IGN and GamingBolt both name:

  • Secrets at the Heart of the Lake - the Meigu Lake mirror Tale. Collect all four Acolyte masks, take a boat to the western edge of the lake, pass through the mirror and clear the realm inside.
  • Bloodline Awakening - find and destroy five Lóng Pillars, each guarded by the Gold-Masked One. The fights get harder as the story advances and you have to win every one.

Because the pillar fights scale with progress, players who leave this to the endgame face the hardest version of five duels back to back. Polygon's recommendation is to do the pillars as you pass them.

sections.title: Final Battle - the True Ending
sections.content:
The true ending is not a choice, it is a checklist. Clear the purple Tales and the item requirements before the point of no return and a second boss fight appears after the regular final boss. Win that, and you get the With Heart and Blood trophy.

The long version - every Tale, every mask, every pillar, and the mistakes that quietly void the whole thing - is on the true ending checklist. The short version:

  • All purple Tales, including the missable ones in Pangzhen, done before the Mirage Estate
  • Both Crystal Puppet Eyes - one from the Mountain of Imprisonment, one from the Crimson Manor secret boss
  • Four Acolyte masks from four scarecrow fights, taken to the mirror at Meigu Lake
  • Five Lóng Pillars, including the one inside the Four Guardians' Mirror realm
  • Quick Hand Zhang's fetch requests, all of them

sections.title: Undying Grudge - the Ending You Get by Losing
sections.content:
The fourth ending is the strangest thing in the game. Finish the story once at any difficulty and 66 Days unlocks - a mode that gives you 66 lives for the whole run. Run out and it is a permanent game over: the save is deleted, not reloaded.

Let that happen and you get Undying Grudge, a unique cutscene that no other route shows. It is the only ending that requires a separate playthrough, and the only one you cannot reach by being good at the game. This site has not seen the cutscene itself and is not going to describe it second-hand - the existence and trigger condition are what IGN and the Chinese guides both confirm.

sections.title: What Actually Voids the True Ending
sections.content:
Three failure modes come up repeatedly in the guides, and all three are silent - the game does not tell you that a Tale has expired.

MistakeWhy it costs you
Doing the purple Tales after Mount SoulrendSeveral expire at the point of no return. The endgame warning tells you content will lock - it does not tell you which content.
Skipping the Mountain of ImprisonmentThe region is optional for the story, which makes it easy to walk past. It holds the Yin Crystal Puppet Eye, and without both eyes the Puppet No. 99 step cannot finish.
Taking the endgame warning as proof you failedThe warning appears even when every prerequisite is met. Chinese guide 177xz makes this point explicitly - do not restart a good save because of the prompt.

One more, less obvious: the pillar inside the Four Guardians' Mirror realm sits where you cannot teleport out with bells. Polygon advises clearing it before advancing, because the alternative is a long walk back.

sections.title: Where This Comes From
sections.content:
Ending names and counts: IGN's All Endings and Requirements, cross-checked against Polygon's true-ending guide, GamingBolt's prerequisites guide and VGTimes. The 66 Days save-deletion behaviour is described the same way by IGN and VGTimes. Chinese-language confirmation of the secret ending's name, 饮恨江湖, comes from the same guides and matches the pre-launch material this site already published.

Not confirmed: whether Long Roar and Final Battle share a cutscene, how many variants exist within each ending, and whether any ending is difficulty-gated. Nothing found suggests difficulty affects the ending.
